note.en: The lapel instead of the sleeve.
A collar and lapel grip is allowed with a positive attitude. Used with one or both arms to force a bending posture, it draws a shido.

about.en: Both hands on the lapels at chest height. Nothing controls the sleeve, so nothing controls the arm, but both hands lift and both pull, and a partner can be moved straight forwards and backwards with great force: the lifting-pulling hip throw and the two inner reaps come from it, and the circle throw when they push back.

en: Both grips at chest height, elbows down
Push and pull with the whole body, not the arms
Attack at once; two lapels held still is a stalling grip
Take one lapel with each hand at chest height, thumbs outside the cloth.
Draw the elbows in so your forearms lie against your partner's chest.
Move them forwards or backwards along the line of the lapels, and attack the moment they resist.

receiving.en: Both lapels held and your sleeves free means pressure straight through your centre. Take a sleeve at once: their arms are the lever and the sleeve is where you stop it.

viNotes.en: Two hands on your chest and none on your arm is a grip you can identify at once. Expect to be moved straight along your own centre line.
